reproduction: Let A_n={0 connected to vertex boundary of [-n,n]^d}. A_{n+1} subset A_n by truncating an open path at its first hit of the smaller boundary. The intersection says the 0-cluster meets every box boundary, equivalent to an infinite cluster on locally finite Z^d. Probability continuity from above gives theta(p)=lim_n P_p(A_n).
remaining_gap: No quantitative bound on P_pc(A_n); does not resolve C0023.

reproduction: The inside-box event equals the unrestricted connection-to-boundary event by stopping at the first boundary hit. For p_k down to p, monotonicity gives theta(p_k)>=theta(p), while theta(p_k)<=a_n(p_k) for each n; finite polynomial continuity gives limsup theta(p_k)<=a_n(p), and infimum over n equals theta(p).
remaining_gap: Right-continuity at p_c does not imply theta(p_c)=0; left-continuity or a direct critical one-arm decay bound remains unproved.

reproduction: Color m sites by residues modulo R+1 in both coordinates. A largest class has at least ceil(m/(R+1)^2) members. Distinct members are at distance >=R+1, so strong sigma-field independence inductively gives mutual independence. All m bad implies that class bad, giving q to its cardinality.
remaining_gap: No estimate when R increases with the block scale.

reproduction: The outer contour of the polyomino made of squares at a finite connected good component maps to a closed star-walk of exterior bad sites. Its nonzero winding forces a simple bad star-cycle. A length-m cycle lies in [-m,m]^2, and overcounting gives (2m+1)^2 8^m. L1 bounds its bad probability by q^(m/K). Sum <=9t(1+t)/(1-t)^3; with t<=0.01 and q<=1/800, total error <0.1.
remaining_gap: The planar contour is a handwritten topological argument, not a formal receipt; no critical block error bound follows.

scope: fixed finite L,M and strict block-error margin
reproduction: D_w(M) is inside D_z(M+L) for each coarse neighbor w; the single global rule defines h_w in both events. G_z uses exactly at most d(2H)(2H+1)^(d-1) internal bonds in D_z(H). If coarse index distance exceeds floor(2H/L), the boxes are disjoint. Uniform coupling gives |P_p(G)-P_p'(G)|<=N|p-p'|, preserving a strict margin at some p'<p. L2 then yields an unbounded compatible anchor cluster and theta(p')>0 by translation invariance.
remaining_gap: At p_c no strict margin is produced; G remains unproved.

scope: iterated limit under an almost surely unique infinite cluster
reproduction: At fixed L each seed contains finitely many candidate vertices. Finite-cluster candidates eventually fail the outer-boundary test; infinite-cluster candidates pass for every sufficiently large M. Hence each lex-first anchor stabilizes. If all five seeds hit the unique infinite cluster, finitely many connecting paths eventually fit the expanded box; otherwise some anchor is undefined. Bounded convergence gives the fixed-L limit, and seed boxes exhaust Z^d as L grows.
remaining_gap: Order of limits is M then L; this gives no dependence-matched finite pair.

reproduction: For fixed L, q_fake(M) drops from 1 to 2^-L at M=L 2^L, so the iterated limit is zero. Before the drop it exceeds the threshold. After it, R=floor(2(M+L)/L)>=2^(L+1)+2, so 800^(-(R+1)^2)<2^-L=q_fake. This disproves the proposed inference from an iterated limit alone.

fixed_statement: There is a decreasing sequence A_n of coordinatewise increasing cylinder events whose probability limit vanishes for p<1/2 but is at least 253/256 at p=1/2.
reproduction: For p<1/2 the strong law eventually violates the moving threshold k/2-2k^(2/3). At p=1/2 Hoeffding gives each failure probability <=exp(-8k^(1/3)); summing by the decreasing-integrand bound gives 3/256. Each A_n is increasing in the coordinatewise order but A_{n+1} is a subset of A_n; the original phrase 'increasing nested' can be read backwards.
remaining_gap: This is a product-event counterexample, not a lattice percolation example.

scope: counterexample only to pointwise first-relay conditional bound
reproduction: With X,Y,Z iid fair edges on o-a2-b-a1, F2={X=1 and not(Y=Z=1)} has probability (1/2)(3/4)=3/8. Intersecting Y=1 forces Z=0, probability 1/8, so the conditional is 1/3. Both relay-to-b marginals are 1/2. The global Kozma-Nitzan inequality remains equality because P(o reaches A)=1/2 and P(o reaches b)=1/4.
remaining_gap: The weighted global comparison is not refuted or independently proved.

scope: stationary finite-dependent correlated field, with range varying by epsilon
reproduction: Good(v) depends on seeds in B_(R+1)(v); translates preserve the lexicographic tie rule, and sets at separation >2(R+1) are independent. A good path has one seed label s, hence lies in B_R(s). If nearest seed distance r<=R-1 and no second seed lies in B_(r+2)(v), all neighbors choose the same seed. Union bound over ordered seed pairs yields formula (1). Shell sizes are bounded by 2d(2r+1)^(d-1) and 6d(2r+5)^(d-1), giving the stated C_d; the integral substitution yields q^(1/d), so choose q small then R large.
remaining_gap: The field is correlated, with R growing as epsilon shrinks; it is not an iid critical-percolation counterexample.
